exercise.name: Cable Standing Side Bend

reference.title: Cable Standing Side Bend (version 3)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.laterality: Unilateral load (one side at a time)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you bend toward the pulley, exhale as you pull back up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s down, short pause, about 1.5 s up

prescription.tempo: About 1.5 s down, brief pause, 1.5 s up
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack. Many coaches prefer suitcase carries for the same muscles with less spine bending.

cues.text: Stand side-on to the low pulley, feet hip width, a D-handle in the right (near) hand at your side, palm facing the thigh; left fingertips lightly behind the head. Step far enough away that the cable is taut.
Breathe in and let the cable draw you straight sideways toward the pulley; the handle slides down the outside of the thigh.
Short pause at a comfortable stretch; no leaning forward or twisting.
Breathe out and pull the trunk back up with the opposite side of the waist, just past upright.
Stand tall; finish the set, then turn around and work the other side.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning forward or twisting toward the stack
mistakes.fix: Move in a flat side plane, chest facing forward.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the handle up with the arm
mistakes.fix: Arm long and relaxed; the waist does the work.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the cable yank you into the bottom
mistakes.fix: Lower over about 1.5 s against the cable.

mistakes.mistake: Standing so close that the cable goes slack at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Step away until the stack lifts slightly at the start.

kinematics.norm: A comfortable side bend toward the pulley and back to just past upright; no study fixes the range (clinical opinion)
Slides down the outside of the thigh, arm vertical (clinical opinion)
Low pulley out to the side, so the cable pulls the trunk toward it through the whole range (clinical opinion)
Square, with a small shift away from the bend (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Standing Side Bend (version 3), video (movement reference)
Konrad, Schmitz and Denner 2001, neuromuscular evaluation of trunk-training exercises (J Athl Train 36(2):109-118; PMC155519)
McGill, Juker and Kropf, quantitative intramuscular myoelectric activity of quadratus lumborum during a wide variety of tasks (Clinical Biomechanics)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Choose a cable load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Low-back pain with side bending: try a suitcase hold or carry (no bend) instead (clinical opinion).
Keep the range comfortable; repeated end-range bending under load is not needed.
modify: Free hand on the hip instead of behind the head.

muscleNotes.obliques_l: The obliques on the side away from the pulley lower the trunk toward it under control and pull it back up; side-lying lateral flexion gave about 98% MVC external oblique in Konrad 2001 (no study measured the cable version).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Quadratus lumborum and the erector spinae opposite the load work with the obliques; quadratus lumborum is a primary lateral stabiliser of the spine (McGill, Juker and Kropf).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: The obliques on the pulley side finish the movement just past upright (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and the deep abdominals keep the trunk from leaning forward or twisting (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Keep the loaded shoulder from being pulled down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level over the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level over the feet (clinical opinion).
